The journey

Voices from the dark

Jonah and Job

One calls from the darkness and one from his pain, and God answers both.

Jonah, the man of the fish, went away in anger. From the darkness he called: there is no god but You, and he owned his wrong. God saved him from his distress. He was sent to a hundred thousand or more, and they believed. Job called that harm had touched him, and that his Lord was the most merciful. God lifted the harm, and gave him back his family and as many more.

﴿وَذَا ٱلنُّونِ إِذ ذَّهَبَ مُغَـٰضِبًا فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ فَنَادَىٰ فِى ٱلظُّلُمَـٰتِ أَن لَّآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَـٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ٨٧ فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ وَنَجَّيْنَـٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ ۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُـۨجِى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ٨٨﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [mention] the man of the fish [i.e., Jonah], when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree [anything] upon him. And he called out within the darknesses, "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers." So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers.

Quran · Al-Anbiya 21:87-88

﴿وَأَرْسَلْنَـٰهُ إِلَىٰ مِا۟ئَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ١٤٧ فَـَٔامَنُوا۟ فَمَتَّعْنَـٰهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ١٤٨﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We sent him to [his people of] a hundred thousand or more. And they believed, so We gave them enjoyment [of life] for a time.

Quran · As-Saffat 37:147-148

﴿وَأَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّى مَسَّنِىَ ٱلضُّرُّ وَأَنتَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ٨٣ فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ فَكَشَفْنَا مَا بِهِۦ مِن ضُرٍّ ۖ وَءَاتَيْنَـٰهُ أَهْلَهُۥ وَمِثْلَهُم مَّعَهُمْ رَحْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِنَا وَذِكْرَىٰ لِلْعَـٰبِدِينَ٨٤﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [mention] Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful." So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of adversity. And We gave him [back] his family and the like thereof with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers [of Allāh].

Quran · Al-Anbiya 21:83-84

You might ask

QuestionWhy did Job's prayer not ask for anything?
AnswerHe named his pain and named God's mercy, and stopped there. The verse shows a prayer that leaves the rest to God.Quran · Al-Anbiya 21:83
QuestionCan I call on God after running away?
AnswerJonah did, from the darkest place in the story. He admitted his wrong, and God answered. The next verse adds that He saves believers in the same way.Quran · Al-Anbiya 21:87-88
QuestionIs suffering a sign that God has left me?
AnswerGod praises Job as an excellent servant, and still harm touched him. In this story pain is no proof of distance from God.Quran · Sad 38:44

Both call on God directly, and Jonah says it in the dark: no god but You.
